decontamination_notes: Real integer-overflow denial-of-service fix from toml-rs/toml PR #1189 ('fix(writer): Don't overflow', fixes #1188), merged 2026-07-14 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. When toml_writer serializes a string it scans for the longest run of consecutive single/double quote characters (to choose the quote style). The run counters (ValueMetrics.max_seq_single_quotes / max_seq_double_quotes) are u8 and each run character is added with an unchecked `+= 1`, so a value with 256+ consecutive quote characters overflows the counter -- a panic in a debug build (DoS from a single serialized string). The fix accumulates the run with core::num::Saturating so it can never overflow. This task slices the standalone, zero-dependency toml_writer crate (restructured to a single crate at the repo root with a minimal Cargo.toml; no vendoring needed) and runs on the :rust image; hidden tests use the public ToTomlValue API. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (1.1k LOC; the counters still using plain `+= 1`); MIT/Apache-2.0 LICENSEs preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (256 double-quotes -> literal '...'; 256 single-quotes -> basic "..."; 300 double-quotes -> literal; each overflows and panics at base) plus a 2-check regression guard (ordinary short strings still serialize as basic strings).
